subject: Running INLA from within the server problems

messages.author: a860e462befdcbf7
messages.subject: Running INLA from within the server problems
parts:
Hi All,

I'm running some long and memory consuming models, which run fine. I use a linux server, and I use inla(...,inla.call = 'submit',...) or (...,inla.call = 'remote',...)
and they use multiple cores. However, in need of speed, I have access to other linux servers where I would like to run some other models. 

So, first, is there a way to configure more than one server for the inla remote/submit call? 

Since I didn't find this, I went ahead and just ran INLA within the server (opened R from within the server and ran INLA). However, it seems that inla is not properly 
taking advantage of all the cores/RAM in the server. Looking at 'top', there is no "inla64" running, just R using a single core. Because of the memory 
requirements, it crashes early on with:

Error: C stack usage  10188999 is too close to the limit   


Any ideas on how to solve this?

R version in server:
 R version 3.1.2 (2014-10-31)

Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit)


INLA version on server:

INLA_0.0-1420281647


Any help would be much appreciated,

Ignacio

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Running INLA from within the server problems
parts:
On Thu, 2015-04-30 at 08:11 -0700, ignacio quintero wrote:

>
> So, first, is there a way to configure more than one server for the
> inla remote/submit call?

Hi,

I have been waiting years for this question... By now, only one remote
host is defined, and I do not know (have not decided) how to extend it.
If someone has suggestions, please let me know.

one option is to extend the call as

inla(..., inla.call = "remote@host")

which will use ~/.inlarc-host, and simular with 'submit' and those. this
gives a lot of files, maybe better to let remote@host define a
variable, like INLAHOST and peple can then make the ~/.inlarc file
depend on it, like

case $INLAHOST in ...
esac

which would require shell-scripting knowledge (in (ba)sh shell).

well, until we decide, you can always use this workaround...

Sys.setenv(INLAHOST="hostname")
r = inla(..., inla.call = "remote")

and then the variable INLAHOST is defined when ~/.inlarc in sourced, so
you can switch of 'if' there, to chost host.

> Since I didn't find this, I went ahead and just ran INLA within the
> server (opened R from within the server and ran INLA). However, it
> seems that inla is not properly
> taking advantage of all the cores/RAM in the server. Looking at 'top',
> there is no "inla64" running, just R using a single core.
seems like it hasn't come the inla64-part yet.

> Because of the memory
> requirements, it crashes early on with:
>
> Error: C stack usage 10188999 is too close to the limit

maybe you need

ulimit -s unlimited

in your .bashrc or something, to set the stack-limit to 'unlimited'.
Maybe this the issue?

H
